status.numerical_agreement_basis: Assessed on all nine in-scope Table III targets, every one of which produced a comparable value from the paper's stated protocol (random 80:20 image split of 69,600/17,400, online training augmentation, fixed tenfold offline validation augmentation to 174,000 images). Comparability was decided on specification grounds before the differences were inspected. The nine differences separate cleanly by split. The four checkpoint-training accuracies are within 1.2146 points (-1.2146, -1.1086, +0.3555, +0.6157). All five augmented-validation accuracies are far above the paper and all in the same direction: +14.4989, +11.4275, +14.3705, +13.7111 and +11.6584 points. Because the contract requires does_not_agree when any assessed value disagrees, the record is does_not_agree; no score-matching tolerance is asserted and no significance test was performed. The one bounded split diagnostic (first 80 percent of lexicographically sorted filenames per class, never substituted for a target result) lowered validation accuracy but left it 9.60 to 10.17 points above Table III, so split order alone does not account for the validation gap; the author split, the saved offline validation images, convolution padding and optimizer remain material unknowns. The four RBF-SVM targets additionally rest on an unreported feature layer and unreported C and gamma, recorded as scikit-learn defaults (C=1, gamma='scale') chosen to avoid score tuning rather than attributed to the authors.
